_version.author: Ash Higgins
source_refs: SJ-21 / SJ-25 RPO and Docking Event AAR
Live Fly 25-2 and 26-1 after action reports
JCO Weekly Activity Reports, 76 editions, via behaviour-library.json
JCO Quick Reference Card, P&D primary sorting
_version.redaction_note: Historical basis fields reference publicly reported events and are generalised. Generated scenarios use synthetic objects with fictitious identifiers; dataMode is set to SIMULATED or EXERCISE on all generated records. No live watchlist membership is encoded.

_design_note: Every template holds the expected response fixed and randomises the instantiation. Each carries at least one distractor trigger event, because a scenario in which every anomaly is real trains over-reporting. Solvability is asserted before a scenario is served: if the expected response cannot be reached from the data available in that seed, the seed is rejected rather than scored.

scenario_templates.name: Something moved
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: You are on shift. A provider has posted a residual plot on an object under standing tasking and flagged a possible manoeuvre. Work the event.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Generic manoeuvre detection and characterisation as taught in JCO continuation training. No single event.

varies: burn direction
burn magnitude
epoch age of the state
observation density either side
which artefact is present, if any
time of day and collection geometry
whether pattern of life supports routine station-keeping
resulting geometry relative to nearby objects
fixed: the procedure
the reporting obligation
the order of the first two steps

trigger_events.event: A residual departure is presented with a possible manoeuvre label from the provider.
expected_response: Check epoch age of the state
Check observation density either side of the departure
acceptable_alternatives: Request observations covering the period before assessing

trigger_events.event: The residual component is visible and identifies in-plane or out-of-plane.
expected_response: State whether the burn is in-plane or out-of-plane
Infer the candidate burn directions from that

trigger_events.event: A DC table is delivered.
expected_response: Read the Delta column
Name the burn direction from the element signature
Sanity-check the delta-v against the altitude change

trigger_events.event: On some seeds, the reported drift rate is physically impossible because the two states have a near-zero epoch separation.
expected_response: Reject the derived rate
Check epoch separation of the inputs
Request states with a usable separation

trigger_events.event: On some seeds, the manoeuvre is entirely consistent with the object's established station-keeping cadence.
expected_response: Compare against pattern of life
Assess as routine and report on that basis rather than as a manoeuvre of intent

trigger_events.event: Reporting decision point.
expected_response: State possible or verified with confidence
Include time, delta-v, period, perigee, apogee, inclination and drift rate
State the resulting geometry and any affected objects
State collection limitations

required_data: residual series with the stated departure
DC table consistent with the seeded burn
pattern of life history of at least four cycles
solvability.check: The seeded burn direction must be recoverable from the DC table Delta column alone, and the pattern of life history must be long enough to support or refute a routine assessment.

scenario_templates.name: Closing on the belt
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: An object of interest has been drifting along the belt for several days. Predictive surveillance has flagged an upcoming crossing. Work the event as it develops.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Patterned on publicly reported GEO rendezvous and proximity behaviour, including sustained perching by collection platforms and multi-week approach sequences between two co-located objects.

varies: drift rate and whether it is slowing
plane relationship and whether deltas are closing
relative motion geometry: natural, forced, drifting or perch
standoff distance held
which phenomenologies are available
whether cross-tagging occurs
collection gaps from eclipse and exclusion
whether the target is red or blue
fixed: the procedure
the escalation obligation on a precision plane match
the requirement to report before the picture is complete

trigger_events.event: A waterfall shows two traces converging in longitude.
expected_response: Request a neighbourhood constrained by inclination and RAAN
State that longitude convergence alone is not proximity

trigger_events.event: The neighbourhood shows inclination and RAAN deltas. On some seeds these are precision matched and held.
expected_response: Verify epoch ages first
Assess the plane relationship
On a precision match, notify higher headquarters promptly and maximise tasking

trigger_events.event: A TRIC plot is delivered showing the relative motion geometry.
expected_response: Classify natural, forced, drifting or perch
Classify the RPO phase
State whether fuel is being spent to maintain the geometry

trigger_events.event: On some seeds, the objects converge close enough that optical merges them while RF still separates them.
expected_response: Assess as unresolved rather than docked
State that cross-tagging is expected at this separation
Report the ambiguity rather than the conclusion

trigger_events.event: On some seeds the object of interest and the object approached are both red.
expected_response: Report anyway
State that practising against an own-nation asset is a recognised precursor

trigger_events.event: Reporting decision point with an incomplete picture.
expected_response: Publish without waiting for completeness
State type, phase, separation, POCA, plane relationship and delta-v assessment
State confidence and what would change it
State collection limitations

required_data: waterfall with at least five days
neighbourhood with epoch ages and plane deltas
TRIC with POCA and RIC components
solvability.check: The seeded RPO type must be unambiguously recoverable from the TRIC across the number of revolutions plotted, and the plane relationship must be recoverable from the neighbourhood.

scenario_templates.name: Now there are two
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: A tracking attempt on a single object has returned more than one. Establish what has happened and take the right path.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Patterned on publicly reported sub-satellite deployments from long-lived parent platforms, and on fragmentation events detected through photometric expansion.

varies: headcount, two or three or more
parent state of behaviour, red or blue
whether a parent manoeuvre is co-timed
whether the new object manoeuvres afterwards
whether the headcount is genuine or a tracking artefact
how far into the parent's life the release falls
whether an unranked object sits inside the threat geometry
collection geometry and gaps
fixed: the branch logic
the requirement to confirm headcount across passes
the differing reporting obligations of the three branches

trigger_events.event: A multiple headcount is reported.
expected_response: Confirm the count across more than one pass before committing
Establish whether the parent is red or blue

trigger_events.event: The branch decision must be taken.
expected_response: Three or more to breakup
Two on a red parent to separation
Two on a blue parent to UCT discovery
State that intent can override count

trigger_events.event: On some seeds the apparent second object is a tracking artefact and does not reappear on subsequent passes.
expected_response: Do not commit to a processing path on a single unconfirmed count
State the count as unconfirmed and continue verification

trigger_events.event: Tasking must be set on both objects.
expected_response: State explicitly which rank applies to the parent and which to the new object

trigger_events.event: A neighbourhood is delivered, filtered to ranked objects only on some seeds.
expected_response: Ask what filter was applied
Request the unfiltered or HRR-plus-UCT view
Include any unranked object inside the threat geometry

trigger_events.event: On some seeds the new object performs a manoeuvre after separation.
expected_response: Assess as an active payload
Reassess reach and threat with the new state
Report the verified manoeuvre separately from the separation

required_data: post-separation state series for the new object
solvability.check: The seeded branch must be determinable from the evidence available at the branch point, and where the count is an artefact the subsequent passes must genuinely fail to reproduce it.

scenario_templates.name: No contact
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: An operator has reported losing contact with a satellite and has asked for support. Establish what happened.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Patterned on the publicly reported loss of a geosynchronous communications satellite where the event occurred during solar exclusion and passive radio frequency signals had dropped away.

varies: whether the object is in solar exclusion
whether passive RF has dropped
time until the next optical pass
fragment count growth rate
energy of the event and therefore Gabbard spread
whether prior anomaly indicators exist
cause: failure, collision, shedding or intercept
fixed: the requirement to establish collection geometry before interpreting absence
the requirement to report headcount as a floor
the handover obligation

trigger_events.event: No signal and no recent observations.
expected_response: Establish whether the object is in solar exclusion or eclipse
State that absence during predicted exclusion is not evidence

trigger_events.event: A pass schedule is available.
expected_response: Identify the next optical visibility window
Increase tasking rank to secure the collection

trigger_events.event: Optical collection returns photometry showing a large expansion in magnitude and a widening spread.
expected_response: Assess as a fragmentation
Use the expansion to bracket the event time
Confirm headcount

trigger_events.event: An early fragment count is available.
expected_response: Report the count as a minimum rather than a total
State that counts grow as the cloud spreads and correlation improves

trigger_events.event: Cause must be assessed.
expected_response: State a cause with confidence from failure, collision, shedding or intercept
Support it with the Gabbard spread, photometric signature and any prior anomaly indicators

trigger_events.event: Closure planning.
expected_response: Plan handover to the cataloguing authority
Maintain coverage of the debris cloud until handover completes
Provide close approach information to affected operators

required_data: collection geometry including exclusion and eclipse windows
fragment states sufficient for a Gabbard diagram
solvability.check: The seeded cause must be distinguishable from at least one alternative using the products available, and the exclusion window must genuinely explain the initial data absence where that seed is used.

scenario_templates.name: The daily sweep
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: It is the start of your shift. Run predictive surveillance across the drifting objects of interest and set the tasking position for the day.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Daily predictive surveillance execution as taught in JCO continuation training.

varies: how many objects are drifting
epoch ages across the neighbourhood
which crossings fall inside the projection window
whether drift is slowing on any object
delta-v cost to close from the current geometry
whether current tasking already aligns with the standard
fixed: the required filters on the neighbourhood request
the order of the analytical steps
the requirement to produce a tasking position even when no change is needed

trigger_events.event: Neighbourhoods must be requested.
expected_response: Apply the required projection window and inclination filter
State that the filters are a requirement, not a preference

trigger_events.event: Neighbourhoods are delivered with mixed epoch ages.
expected_response: Verify epoch ages before assessing any distance
Flag objects whose states are too old to assess

trigger_events.event: Points of closest approach in the window must be identified.
expected_response: Identify each crossing and its time
Confirm the tasking rank of both objects against the standard

trigger_events.event: On some seeds an object's drift is decreasing and it appears to be preparing to park.
expected_response: Raise tasking
Assess the resulting geometry against nearby assets
Treat as a reportable development

trigger_events.event: The daily output must be produced.
expected_response: Request the tasking changes, or state explicitly that current tasking aligns
Record the position for the day

required_data: drift history sufficient to detect a slowing trend
solvability.check: Every seeded crossing must fall inside the projection window, and where drift is seeded as slowing the trend must be detectable across the history provided.

scenario_templates.name: Ninety minutes
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: A cue has arrived indicating a launch on a high-altitude ballistic profile. Operators need warning and the clock is running.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Patterned on the publicly discussed geosynchronous direct ascent test profile and the associated JCO processing timeline.

varies: apogee above or below belt altitude
crossing longitude
quality and timing of the initial cue
when acquisition succeeds
whether a separation is detected
which objects fall inside the initial and refined bands
whether an impact occurs
fixed: the phase structure
the requirement to publish before the picture is good
the requirement not to wait for a solve on separation detection

trigger_events.event: The cue arrives with time, location and azimuth.
expected_response: Determine whether apogee is at or below belt altitude or above it
Select the correct assessment longitude accordingly

trigger_events.event: An initial target list is available across a wide band.
expected_response: Make a verbal notification
Publish an initial report listing blue assets and well-tracked uncorrelated tracks at risk
State that the list may change

trigger_events.event: Acquisition succeeds and a state is generated.
expected_response: Narrow the band
Publish a refined report now including red objects

trigger_events.event: On some seeds, no significant change occurs during the coast phase.
expected_response: Do not republish unchanged information
Continue refining the state

trigger_events.event: On some seeds, a separation is detected.
expected_response: Make an immediate verbal notification
Publish the flash report immediately without waiting for an orbit determination
Follow with the refined target assessment when the solve completes

required_data: initial cue with time, location and azimuth
belt objects with identifiers within the candidate bands
solvability.check: The correct assessment longitude must be determinable from the seeded apogee relationship, and the target list must be non-empty within the seeded band.

scenario_templates.name: More than you can hold
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: Two time-critical events land within minutes of each other while proximity threads are already running. You cannot work all of it properly. Decide what you are not working, and say so.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Patterned on exercise days where near-simultaneous direct ascent events with concurrent proximity threads drove first report latency past an hour and peak concurrent thread counts to around thirty-five.

varies: how many events arrive and how close together
which threads are already ripe at start
which threads are resolved but still open
whether a mandatory notification is outstanding
which provider is degraded
the order in which evidence arrives
fixed: that the load exceeds capacity
that triage is scored
that latency runs from indication rather than from noticing

trigger_events.event: Two time-critical indications arrive within minutes, with proximity threads already open.
expected_response: Publish a holding alert on each time-critical event inside minutes
Do not serialise the two

trigger_events.event: Thread load now exceeds what can be actively worked.
expected_response: Triage explicitly into active, monitoring and ready to close
Order by the published event priority rather than by recency or by which arrived loudest
State what is not being worked

trigger_events.event: Some open threads are resolved and consuming attention.
expected_response: Close the resolved threads deliberately

trigger_events.event: A ripe proximity thread has sat untouched since before the surge began.
expected_response: Sweep for untouched threads
Action or explicitly defer it with a reason

trigger_events.event: On some seeds, one of the concurrent events is a routine station-keep that does not warrant escalation.
expected_response: Assess as routine
Do not spend surge capacity on it

required_data: open thread list with last activity times
pattern of life history for the routine seed
solvability.check: Total workable capacity must be genuinely exceeded, and at least one thread must be closable and one ripe, so triage has a correct answer.

triage_authority.source: Quick Reference Card, P&D primary sorting
triage_authority.note: Triage is now scored against the published priority order rather than against authoring judgement. This was previously a gap: the scenario scored triage with no authoritative order behind it.

scenario_templates.name: Consequence first
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: Evidence of an outcome has arrived and nothing explains it yet. Work it.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Patterned on an exercise day where a debris cloud report preceded the launch confirmation that explained it, causing confusion and slowing situational awareness.

varies: how long the explaining indication is delayed
whether it arrives at all
whether attention is already committed to another event
the true cause among failure, collision, shedding and intercept
collection geometry
fixed: that the consequence arrives before the cause
that the effect procedure governs

trigger_events.event: Fragmentation evidence arrives with no indication of a cause.
expected_response: Start the procedure governing the effect
Do not wait for the expected trigger

trigger_events.event: Reasoning backwards to a likely cause.
expected_response: Generate candidate causes
Check timing and geometry for a plausible causal link

trigger_events.event: On some seeds a related indication arrives late and confirms the link.
expected_response: Connect it to the running event rather than opening a new one
Execute the transition deliberately and state what carries across

trigger_events.event: On some seeds the late indication is unrelated and coincidental.
expected_response: Test the causal link before connecting them
Keep them separate and say why

solvability.check: The causal link must be testable from timing and geometry, and on coincidental seeds must be genuinely refutable.

scenario_templates.name: What they did not tell you
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: You have just taken the handover. Get the picture straight, then work it.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Patterned on exercise handovers of varying quality, including one delayed by late arrivals and followed by slow inject pickup, and cases where indications present on the previous shift were not transitioned until the following one.

varies: how complete the brief is
how many open threads are omitted
whether an omitted thread is ripe or resolved
whether an untransitioned trigger sits on a previous shift's thread
how stale the states are
fixed: that the brief is reconcilable against the open thread list
that latency on an inherited ripe thread runs from when the trigger appeared

trigger_events.event: A handover brief covering most but not all open threads.
expected_response: Reconcile the briefed set against the open record
Identify events not covered
Check each briefed event against the six-point standard, particularly next step and current checklist position

trigger_events.event: An omitted thread carries an untransitioned proximity trigger from the previous shift.
expected_response: Transition it immediately
Recognise that the clock started when the trigger appeared, not at handover

trigger_events.event: On some seeds another omitted thread is fully resolved.
expected_response: Close it
Do not spend attention re-establishing a finished picture

trigger_events.event: End of shift approaches with work outstanding.
expected_response: Brief each open event against the six points
State next steps and current checklist step for each
Ensure every open thread carries a timer and every elevation an expiry

required_data: full open thread list with last activity
solvability.check: Every omitted thread must be discoverable by reconciling the brief against the thread list, and the untransitioned trigger must be unambiguous once seen.

brief_standard.note: The handover brief is now scored against the published six-point standard rather than against authoring judgement.

scenario_templates.name: Something looks different
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: A provider has flagged a change in an object's light curve. Establish whether it is real, what caused it, and whether it is reportable.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Photometric change is the third most common report type in real reporting volume and among the lowest scoring for quality, with reports frequently precise about the observation and silent on its meaning.

varies: which of the five change signatures is present
whether the change is real or one of the three collection explanations
how many sensors and which hemispheres saw it
whether a close approach falls in the window and whether lighting was favourable
whether a co-timed manoeuvre exists
whether the object is subject to a suppression rule
whether the object carries an Alpha-5 designator
whether the change is consistent with pattern of life
fixed: that suppression rules are checked before analysis
that the three scepticism checks precede any assessment of cause
that phase angle window and magnitudes are required content

trigger_events.event: An indication of photometric change arrives.
expected_response: Check suppression rules before beginning analysis
Check whether the object is docked

trigger_events.event: The light curve is available.
expected_response: Name which of the five change signatures is present
Compare intervals at matched phase angle

trigger_events.event: On some seeds the change is visible on one sensor only, or from a different hemisphere than the rest of the data.
expected_response: Run the three scepticism checks
Request the sensor or hemisphere view
Do not assess as real until corroborated

trigger_events.event: A close approach falls inside the change window.
expected_response: Establish whether lighting was favourable
State time, distance and lighting together
Include or exclude it as the cause explicitly

trigger_events.event: The report must be produced.
expected_response: State phase angle window, magnitude change and direction, and magnitudes before and after
State the assessed cause or state it as unknown
State whether consistent with pattern of life
State longitude and drift rate with direction

required_data: light curve against phase angle across multiple intervals
neighbourhood with close approaches in the window
solvability.check: The seeded cause must be distinguishable from at least one alternative using the products available, and on collection-artefact seeds the supporting view must genuinely eliminate the change.

scenario_templates.name: Window opens
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: A launch is expected. Work it from pre-notice through to whatever it becomes.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Launch is the second most common report type in real reporting volume and among the lowest scoring for quality, with reports frequently reduced to nominals with no assessment.

varies: whether the payload is threat, unknown or non-threat
whether the launch time slips and by how much
whether acquisition succeeds and after how many passes
whether the nominal is correct or wrong in plane
destination regime and whether a transfer is involved
what is in plane or near the destination longitude
whether the launch fails
fixed: that pre-launch, liftoff and initial track are separate reporting obligations
that a candidate track is published on before separation
that a wrong nominal and an absent object look identical

trigger_events.event: Pre-notice indicators arrive with a payload of uncertain character.
expected_response: Determine whether this is processed and on which path
Treat unknown as a reason to process rather than to skip

trigger_events.event: The window opens in a day.
expected_response: Publish the pre-launch report
State expected regime and orbital characteristics
State what is in plane or near the destination

trigger_events.event: On some seeds the launch time slips.
expected_response: Re-rotate the nominal to the new time
Redistribute
Re-run the in-plane or apogee assessment because RAAN has changed

trigger_events.event: A candidate track is obtained before separation.
expected_response: Publish immediately without waiting for identification

trigger_events.event: On some seeds no track is obtained across several passes because the nominal is wrong in plane.
expected_response: Reassess the nominal before concluding the launch failed

trigger_events.event: On some seeds the object is in a parking orbit bound for a higher regime.
expected_response: State current orbit and intended destination separately
Keep the event open across the transfer

required_data: coplanar or neighbourhood assessment for the destination
actual insertion state where acquisition succeeds
solvability.check: Where the nominal is seeded wrong in plane, the error must be recoverable by re-examining the rotation and profile rather than by guessing.

scenario_templates.name: Everything you have
scenario_templates.narrative_frame: Everything available is on the board. Some of it disagrees, some of it is old, and one provider is down. Work out what is happening and be ready to defend it.
scenario_templates.historical_basis: Composite of recorded conditions: provider degradation during exercise activity, stale states in delivered products, varying display conventions, and assessments made under genuine contradiction.

varies: which provider is degraded
which products conflict and whether the conflict is material
how stale each state is
whether the display convention differs from the last delivery
which anatomy question the available evidence cannot answer
the strength of the challenge posed afterwards
fixed: that the board is full
that some contradiction is unresolvable
that an assessment is required regardless
that a challenge follows

trigger_events.event: The full board is presented with degraded elements.
expected_response: Establish what is degraded before reading anything
Check conventions on each product

trigger_events.event: Two products disagree materially.
expected_response: Prefer the product closer to the observations
State which you believe and why

trigger_events.event: On some seeds a contradiction is present that does not change the conclusion.
expected_response: Recognise it as immaterial
Say so rather than resolving it or ignoring it

trigger_events.event: The assessment is due.
expected_response: Conclusion, evidence chain, eliminated alternative, proportionate confidence, falsifier, gaps
Answer all eight anatomy questions from evidence

trigger_events.event: A challenge is posed to the assessment.
expected_response: Defend with evidence, or revise where the challenge is good

required_data: full product set with degradation metadata
conflicting pair with a determinable resolution
evidence sufficient for at least six of eight anatomy questions
solvability.check: A defensible conclusion must be reachable despite the contradictions, and at least one anatomy question must be genuinely unanswerable so the gaps statement has something to contain.

_behaviour_library_link.note: Scenario generators draw behavioural realism from behaviour-library.json rather than inventing it. Each archetype supplies quantified norms for manoeuvre magnitudes, approach distances, pattern of life cadences and multi-object choreography, generalised from two years of weekly reporting.
_behaviour_library_link.requirement: Every scenario seed that involves an object of interest should draw its behavioural profile from an archetype, so that pattern of life comparison has something real to compare against. A generated object with no history cannot support the pattern of life assessment that most report types require.
_behaviour_library_link.tempo: Seeds should carry running events alongside new ones, and some should present an event whose meaningful history began months earlier. A trainer composed entirely of fresh events teaches a tempo that does not exist.
